newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea prices off on big volumes,poor quality.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea prices off on big volumes,poor quality.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea prices fell across the board at the Colombo auction because of bigger volumes, lower quality and less demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), brokers said on Wednesday.
"This was perhaps one of the largest sales we've had," said a broker. "Larger volumes are on offer in the sales ahead."
Brokers Forbes and Walker said the anticipated gross auction average fell to 107 rupees per kg for the 5.4 million kg on offer as against 111.11 rupees last week.
Buying by the CIS, Sri Lanka's main tea market, had slowed because the winter rush was over, brokers said.
"Quality is also on the decline," another broker said. "Coupled with restricted demand from the CIS this resulted in a drop in prices."
The next auction is on November 19-20 when 5.4 million kg will be on offer. ($1=Rs.56.92)
